content: 1. Salicylic acid may be displaced from protein-binding sites or may displace other protein-bound drugs, potentially enhancing the effects of the displaced drug. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases serum potassium levels, while pirbuterol decreases them. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, so caution and close monitoring are recommended. 3. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and piroxicam both increase anticoagulation and serum potassium levels. Close monitoring is necessary. 4. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases the levels or effects of piroxicam by competing for renal tubular clearance as an acidic (anionic) drug. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 5. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and potassium acid phosphate both increase serum potassium levels. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 6. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and potassium chloride both increase serum potassium levels. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 7. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and potassium citrate both increase serum potassium levels. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 8. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases pralatrexate levels by reducing renal clearance. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 9. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and prasugrel may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 10. The concurrent use of low-dose aspirin with anticoagulants or antiplatelet agents is common in patients with cardiovascular disease. Close monitoring is essential. 11. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate reduces the effects of prazosin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 12. NSAIDs, including aspirin, reduce prostaglandin synthesis, which may affect fluid homeostasis and diminish the antihypertensive effects of certain drugs. Close monitoring is necessary. 13. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and prednisolone may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 14. Prednisolone reduces the levels of aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 15. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and prednisone may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 16. Prednisone reduces the levels of aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 17. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate reduces the effects of probenecid through acidic (anionic) drug competition for renal tubular clearance. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. 18. Aspirin reduces the uricosuric action of probenecid. Close monitoring is necessary. 19. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate reduces the effects of propranolol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 20. Long-term NSAID use, including aspirin, may increase serum potassium levels when combined with propranolol. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 21. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and protamine both increase anticoagulation. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 22. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and quinapril may increase each other's toxicity through unspecified mechanisms. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 23. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate reduces the effects of quinapril through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 24. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and ramipril may increase each other's toxicity through unspecified mechanisms. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 25. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate reduces the effects of ramipril through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 26. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and reishi both increase anticoagulation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 27. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and reteplase may increase each other's toxicity through anticoagulation. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 28. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of rilpivirine by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 29. Co-administration of antacids with rilpivirine may significantly reduce rilpivirine plasma concentrations due to increased gastric pH. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 30. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of riociguat by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are recommended, with administration separated by at least 1 hour. 31. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and rivaroxaban may increase each other's toxicity through anticoagulation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 32. Aspirin is known to increase bleeding risk, which may be further elevated when used with rivaroxaban. Monitor for signs and symptoms of blood loss. 33. Rivastigmine increases the toxicity of aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially leading to increased gastrointestinal symptoms. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 34. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of rose hips by increasing renal clearance. Conversely, rose hips increase the levels of aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 35. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and sacubitril/valsartan may increase each other's toxicity through unspecified mechanisms. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 36. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate reduces the effects of sacubitril/valsartan through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 37. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and salicylates (non-ASA) both increase anticoagulation and serum potassium levels. Close monitoring is necessary. 38. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases the levels or effects of salicylates (non-ASA) by competing for renal tubular clearance as an acidic (anionic) drug. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 39. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases serum potassium levels, while salmeterol decreases them. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, so caution and close monitoring are recommended. 40. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and salsalate both increase anticoagulation and serum potassium levels. Close monitoring is necessary. 41. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases the levels or effects of salsalate by competing for renal tubular clearance as an acidic (anionic) drug. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 42. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels or effects of sarecycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 43. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair the absorption of tetracyclines, reducing their efficacy. Separate the dosing of tetracyclines from these products. 44. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and sertraline may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of upper gastrointestinal bleeding. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 45. SSRIs, such as sertraline, inhibit serotonin uptake by platelets, which may contribute to an increased bleeding risk when combined with aspirin. 46. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and Siberian ginseng both increase anticoagulation. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 47. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate reduces the effects of silodosin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 48. Sodium bicarbonate increases salicylate levels at moderate doses but decreases them at high doses due to increased renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 49. Sodium citrate/citric acid increases salicylate levels at moderate doses but decreases them at high doses due to increased renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 50. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid may increase each other's toxicity through fluid and electrolyte imbalances. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 51. Co-administration of medications causing fluid and electrolyte abnormalities may increase the risk of adverse events such as seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Close monitoring is necessary. 52. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 53. Velpatasvir solubility decreases as gastric pH increases, becoming practically insoluble at pH > 5. Separate the administration of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir from antacids by at least 4 hours. 54. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate reduces the effects of sotalol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 55. Long-term NSAID use, including aspirin, may increase serum potassium levels when combined with sotalol. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 56. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels or effects of sotorasib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 57. If co-administration with an acid-reducing agent cannot be avoided, administer sotorasib 4 hours before or 10 hours after a locally-acting antacid. 58. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate reduces the effects of sparsentan by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 59. Antacids may decrease sparsentan exposure, potentially reducing its efficacy. Administer sparsentan 2 hours before or after antacids. 60. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate reduces the effects of spironolactone through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 61. Spironolactone and aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate both increase serum potassium levels. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 62. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases streptomycin levels by reducing renal clearance. This interaction mainly occurs in preterm infants. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 63. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and succinylcholine both increase serum potassium levels. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 64. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases sulfadiazine levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 65. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and sulfamethoxazole may increase each other's effects through plasma protein-binding competition. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 66. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 67. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and sulfasalazine both increase anticoagulation and serum potassium levels. Close monitoring is necessary. 68. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases the levels or effects of sulfasalazine by competing for renal tubular clearance as an acidic (anionic) drug. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 69. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases sulfisoxazole levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 70. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and sulindac both increase anticoagulation and serum potassium levels. Close monitoring is necessary. 71. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases the levels or effects of sulindac by competing for renal tubular clearance as an acidic (anionic) drug. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 72. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and telmisartan may increase each other's toxicity through unspecified mechanisms. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 73. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate reduces the effects of telmisartan through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 74. Telmisartan and aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate both increase serum potassium levels. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 75. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and temocillin may increase each other's levels by reducing renal clearance or through plasma protein-binding competition. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 76. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate and tenecteplase may increase each other's toxicity through anticoagulation. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 77. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate increases teniposide levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 78. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate reduces the effects of terazosin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended.
